title: Finite-free map tensors and their least coefficient support
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $P$ a finite free $R$-module, meaning $P\cong R^r$ for a finite integer $r\ge0$. Set $H=\operatorname{Hom}_R(P,R)$, the module of $R$-linear maps. Then $H$ is finite free, and for every $R$-module $N$ the map $\Phi_N:H\otimes_R N\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_R(P,N)$, $h\otimes n\longmapsto(v\longmapsto h(v)n)$, is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For every finite basis $(e_a)$ of $P$ with dual basis $(e_a^*)$, its inverse is $\Phi_N^{-1}(g)=\sum_a e_a^*\otimes g(e_a)$. It is natural in $N$: for $v:N\to N'$ and $z\in H\otimes_R N$, $\Phi_{N'}((1_H\otimes v)z)=v\circ\Phi_N(z)$. Let $E\cong R^s$ be finite free, $u:P\to E$ linear, $z_u=\Phi_E^{-1}(u)$, and $C_u=\operatorname{im}(\operatorname{Hom}_R(E,R)\to H)$, where the map sends $\lambda$ to $\lambda\circ u$. For every submodule $G\subseteq H$, the inclusion-induced map $G\otimes_R E\to H\otimes_R E$ is injective, and $z_u$ belongs to its image if and only if $C_u\subseteq G$. Thus $C_u$ is the least such $G$. More explicitly, for every finite basis $(b_t)$ of $E$ and its dual basis $(b_t^*)$, $z_u=\sum_t(b_t^*\circ u)\otimes b_t$ and $C_u$ is generated by the $b_t^*\circ u$.

source.place: Tag 059S (lemma-flat-ML-criterion), proof: paragraph beginning "Since $M_i$ is free and finite"; natural dual-tensor isomorphism also in Tag 059G (remark-flat-ML).

proof.text: Choose a finite basis $(e_a)$ of $P$, and let $e_a^*:P\to R$ send a vector to its $a$-th coordinate. The coordinate identity $p=\sum_a e_a^*(p)e_a$ gives $h=\sum_a h(e_a)e_a^*$ for every $h\in H$. Evaluating $\sum_a r_ae_a^*=0$ at $e_b$ gives $r_b=0$. Thus $(e_a^*)$ is a finite basis of $H$, so $H$ is finite free. This argument applies to every chosen finite basis of $P$.

proof.text: The map $(h,n)\mapsto(p\mapsto h(p)n)$ is $R$-bilinear, so the universal property of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives the linear map $\Phi_N$ with the stated pure-tensor formula. Define the linear map $\Psi_N:\operatorname{Hom}_R(P,N)\to H\otimes_R N$ by $\Psi_N(g)=\sum_a e_a^*\otimes g(e_a)$; linearity follows by distributing the finite sum and the tensor in its second variable.

source.place: Tag 059G (remark-flat-ML), functorial finite-free dual/tensor identification; Tag 059S (lemma-flat-ML-criterion), proof, paragraph beginning "Since $M_i$ is free and finite", with the omitted basis calculations written out.

proof.text: For every $p\in P$, $\Phi_N\Psi_N(g)(p)=\sum_a e_a^*(p)g(e_a)=g(p)$. On a pure tensor, $\Psi_N\Phi_N(h\otimes n)=\sum_a e_a^*\otimes h(e_a)n=(\sum_a h(e_a)e_a^*)\otimes n=h\otimes n$. Pure tensors generate by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], so these are inverse linear maps. This proves the isomorphism and the inverse formula for every finite basis.

source.place: Tag 059G (remark-flat-ML), functorial finite-free dual/tensor identification; Tag 059S (lemma-flat-ML-criterion), proof, paragraph beginning "Since $M_i$ is free and finite", with the omitted basis calculations written out.

proof.text: For a linear map $v:N\to N^{\prime}$, the bilinear map $(h,n)\mapsto h\otimes v(n)$ induces $1_H\otimes v$ by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. On a pure tensor, both sides of the claimed naturality identity send $p$ to $h(p)v(n)=v(h(p)n)$. Both sides are linear in the tensor variable, so generation by pure tensors proves the identity for every $z$.

source.place: Tag 059G (remark-flat-ML), functorial finite-free dual/tensor identification; Tag 059S (lemma-flat-ML-criterion), proof, paragraph beginning "Since $M_i$ is free and finite", with the omitted basis calculations written out.

proof.text: Choose any finite basis $(b_t)$ of $E$ with coordinate maps $b_t^*$, and put $c_t=b_t^*\circ u$. For every $p$, $\Phi_E(\sum_t c_t\otimes b_t)(p)=\sum_t b_t^*(u(p))b_t=u(p)$, hence $z_u=\sum_t c_t\otimes b_t$ by step 3. Every $c_t$ lies in $C_u$. Conversely, each $\lambda:E\to R$ satisfies $\lambda=\sum_t\lambda(b_t)b_t^*$, whence $\lambda\circ u=\sum_t\lambda(b_t)c_t$. Therefore $C_u$ is exactly the submodule generated by the $c_t$.

source.place: Tag 059G (remark-flat-ML), functorial finite-free dual/tensor identification; Tag 059S (lemma-flat-ML-criterion), proof, paragraph beginning "Since $M_i$ is free and finite", with the omitted basis calculations written out.

proof.text: For $M=G$ and $M=H$, the bilinear formula $(m,e)\mapsto b_t^*(e)m$ induces a linear map $q_t^M:M\otimes_R E\to M$ by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. On $m\otimes e$, the basis identity for $e$ gives $\sum_t q_t^M(m\otimes e)\otimes b_t=\sum_t b_t^*(e)m\otimes b_t=m\otimes e$. Since pure tensors generate, every $w\in M\otimes_R E$ satisfies $w=\sum_t q_t^M(w)\otimes b_t$.

source.place: Tag 059G (remark-flat-ML), functorial finite-free dual/tensor identification; Tag 059S (lemma-flat-ML-criterion), proof, paragraph beginning "Since $M_i$ is free and finite", with the omitted basis calculations written out.

proof.text: Write $i:G\hookrightarrow H$ and $j=i\otimes1_E$. On pure tensors, $q_t^Hj=iq_t^G$, and generation extends this equality to all tensors [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. If $j(w)=0$, then $i(q_t^G(w))=q_t^H(j(w))=0$ for every $t$. Injectivity of $i$ makes every $q_t^G(w)$ zero, so step 6 gives $w=0$. Thus $j$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 059G (remark-flat-ML), functorial finite-free dual/tensor identification; Tag 059S (lemma-flat-ML-criterion), proof, paragraph beginning "Since $M_i$ is free and finite", with the omitted basis calculations written out.

proof.text: If $C_u\subseteq G$, every $c_t$ belongs to $G$, and $\sum_t c_t\otimes b_t$ formed in $G\otimes_R E$ maps to $z_u$ by step 5. Conversely, if $z_u=j(w)$, apply $q_t^H$: steps 5 and 7 give $c_t=q_t^H(z_u)=i(q_t^G(w))\in G$ for every $t$. The generation of $C_u$ in step 5 implies $C_u\subseteq G$. Taking $G=C_u$ proves that $C_u$ supports $z_u$, and the converse proves it is least. Empty bases give empty sums throughout, covering both rank-zero cases.

lean.statement: theorem finite_free_map_coefficient_support (R : Type uR) [CommRing R] (P : Type uP) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.Free R P] [Module.Finite R P] : Module.Free R (Module.Dual R P) ∧ Module.Finite R (Module.Dual R P) ∧ (∀ (N : Type uN) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N], Function.Bijective (dualTensorHom R P N) ∧ (∀ (h : Module.Dual R P) (n : N) (p : P), dualTensorHom R P N (h ⊗ₜ[R] n) p = h p • n) ∧ (∀ (ι : Type uι) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (e : Module.Basis ι R P) (g : P →ₗ[R] N), (dualTensorHomEquiv R P N).symm g = ∑ a, e.dualBasis a ⊗ₜ[R] g (e a))) ∧ (∀ (N : Type uN) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] (N' : Type uN') [AddCommGroup N'] [Module R N'] (v : N →ₗ[R] N') (z : Module.Dual R P ⊗[R] N), dualTensorHom R P N' (v.lTensor (Module.Dual R P) z) = v.comp (dualTensorHom R P N z)) ∧ (∀ (E : Type uE) [AddCommGroup E] [Module R E] [Module.Free R E] [Module.Finite R E] (u : P →ₗ[R] E), (∀ G : Submodule R (Module.Dual R P), Function.Injective (G.subtype.rTensor E) ∧ ((dualTensorHomEquiv R P E).symm u ∈ LinearMap.range (G.subtype.rTensor E) ↔ LinearMap.range u.dualMap ≤ G)) ∧ IsLeast {G : Submodule R (Module.Dual R P) | (dualTensorHomEquiv R P E).symm u ∈ LinearMap.range (G.subtype.rTensor E)} (LinearMap.range u.dualMap) ∧ (∀ (κ : Type uκ) [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] (b : Module.Basis κ R E), (dualTensorHomEquiv R P E).symm u = ∑ t, ((b.dualBasis t).comp u) ⊗ₜ[R] b t ∧ LinearMap.range u.dualMap = Submodule.span R (Set.range (fun t ↦ (b.dualBasis t).comp u))))
